Generate a variable correlated with an existing variable

Source: R/draw_multivariate.R
correlate.Rd

Uses a Gaussian copula to produce a draw from draw_handler whose rank correlation with given is approximately rho. Works with any draw_* function that accepts a quantile_y argument, and with base R random-number generators (e.g. rnorm, rpois).

Usage

correlate(draw_handler, ..., given, rho)

Arguments

draw_handler

Unquoted function name. Either one of the three draw_* functions that take a quantile_y argument (draw_binary, draw_binomial, draw_count) or a base R r* generator with a q* counterpart (rnorm, rpois, rbinom, and the rest of the stats family). draw_ordered, draw_likert, draw_categorical, draw_quantile, and the two ICC draws take no quantile argument and are refused with a message saying so.

...

Arguments forwarded to draw_handler (e.g. prob, mean).

given

Reference vector; the new variable will be rank-correlated with this.

rho

Correlation of the Gaussian copula, in \([-1, 1]\). It is not the realized Spearman correlation, which is smaller by the copula's own relation, \((6/\pi)\arcsin(\rho/2)\): rho = 0.7 lands at 0.68 and rho = 0.3 at 0.288. The realized Pearson correlation is rho. fabricatr 1.x behaves identically.

Value

A double vector of length length(given). Note that the type is double whatever draw_handler is: draw_binary, draw_binomial, and draw_count each return an integer vector when called directly and a double one when routed through here, because the copula reaches them through a quantile function. The values are unaffected. An NA in given yields an NA in the result at that position.

Examples

score  <- rnorm(100, mean = 75, sd = 10)
offers <- correlate(draw_count, mean = 3, given = score, rho = 0.6)
cor(score, offers, method = "spearman")
#> [1] 0.6068749

# Works with base R generators too
y2 <- correlate(rnorm, mean = 0, sd = 1, given = score, rho = -0.5)
